honest_framing: This is STILL A TARGET CHANGE (wide 4-bit readings on random emissions). 2-bit readings at 20 states stay Open. The 060 question is only whether certify/20b's exact identifier, with its declared bound lifted from 20 to 24 (and 32) by a new module, decides fresh 24-state worlds with random 4-bit readings within B 8M, and stays sound at 32. The guarantee is conditional on the declared N (Inferred: a larger machine can copy the true machine on every visited state) and on noise-free readings. Results are for random 4-bit readings on worlds_026 transitions only.
brand: charcoal and sage; no purple, neon, emoji or gold
question: (A) Does brute.certify/32b (certify/20b with the declared size bound owned by the new module, accepted in 1..32) decide (ID+IDF) at least 6 of 12 fresh 24-state worlds with random noise-free 4-bit readings at C 50000, B 8000000, K 400? (B) Does it stay sound (WRONG 0) at 24 and 32 states? (C) Is certify/32b at bounds <= 20 exactly certify/20b? (D) What do 32-state worlds cost and decide at the same budget (reported)?

hypotheses.H1: no record (S24, S24b, S32) is WRONG; ID checked from the start state and IDF from the current state against the true machine
hypotheses.H3: S24 and S24b give byte-identical canonical records on 12/12 seeds (conflict-counted, no wall guard)

design.api: one new module brute/api/certify32b.py (brute.certify/32b): Certifier32B(Certifier20B) calls the certify/20b constructor with min(family_bound, 20) so its argument check passes, then sets self.N = family_bound (1..32) before any query is built; certify16d.A16D_MAX_BOUND is never changed (no global patch). Every other behaviour is certify/20b's. certify/20b, certify/16d and earlier modules are imported only, never edited. Host-agnostic: no I/O, threads, subprocess or os.
design.worlds: experiments/worlds_060.py: for seed s and n in {24, 32}: transitions and start exactly worlds_026.scale_world(s, n); emissions worlds_058.emissions(s, 4, n) (random 4-bit codes); passive prefix worlds_026.actions(s, 0, 3). Exactly the probe's worlds. true_size (Moore refinement) is reported; labels are behaviour-based.

certification_rule: certify/32b becomes certified for read_bits 4 at declared N <= 24 iff every gated criterion passes. If every gate except GN24_60 passes, it is published as sound but not certified. If any other gate fails it has no certification status. N 25..32 gets no certification status from this study whatever S32 shows. certify/20b and earlier statuses are unchanged. 2-bit 20-state worlds stay Open whatever happens.
status_wording_rule: every status phrase in RELEASE.json, README, CHANGELOG, HANDOFF, the tag message and the release notes is derived from the two GATES_060 flags: certified -> 'certified (read_bits 4, N <= 24)'; sound_not_certified -> 'sound but not certified'; neither -> 'not certified, no certification status' plus the failing gates

claim_scope: conditional on the declared N and noise-free readings: an ID or IDF means unique among machines with at most N states consistent with the trace.
